title: South Korean K-Beauty Giant Goodai Global Files for KOSPI Listing Preliminary Review, Targets approximately $7.5 Billion Valuation - BigGo Finance

Mirae Asset Securities is the lead underwriter, with NH Investment & Securities, Citigroup Global Markets Securities and Morgan Stanley as co-underwriters. The offering allocates 28,025,740 shares, about 24% of the shares to be outstanding after listing. The company posted 2025 consolidated revenue of 1.4718 trillion won (approximately $1.1 billion) and operating profit of 273.4 billion won (approximately $204.7 million), and the market is floating valuations of 8 trillion to 10 trillion won (approximately $6.0 billion to approximately $7.5 billion). Goodai Global has halted Kraver Corporation's planned separate listing in Japan and is moving to clean up its governance structure, including buying out financial investors' stakes. Key Elements 
 Goodai Global Joseon Beauty Kraver Corporation Skin1004 Mirae Asset Securities NH Investment & Securities Citigroup Global Markets Securities Morgan Stanley Korea Exchange Tirtir House of Huh Round Lab Skinfood Goodai Global, which has emerged as a leading K-beauty company, has entered the formal process for a listing on South Korea's main KOSPI market. The market's estimated valuation runs as high as 10 trillion won (approximately $7.5 billion), drawing attention to whether a large IPO can emerge in a sluggish new-issue market.
 According to the investment banking industry on the 13th, Goodai Global submitted its preliminary listing review application to the KOSPI Market Division of the Korea Exchange that day. Mirae Asset Securities is the lead underwriter, with NH Investment & Securities, Citigroup Global Markets Securities and Morgan Stanley participating as co-underwriters. Barring any special complications during the review, a KOSPI debut within the first half of next year is expected.
 The offering allocates a total of 28,025,740 shares, about 24% of the 116,773,761 shares expected to be outstanding after listing. The company was valued at 4.4 trillion won (approximately $3.3 billion) when it raised 800 billion won (approximately $598.9 million) in pre-IPO funding through convertible bonds (CBs) in August last year. Industry observers expect the company to aim for a valuation of around 8 trillion to 10 trillion won through this listing.
 Founded in December 2016, Goodai Global achieved results in overseas markets including North America the following year with its own brand Joseon Beauty. It then rapidly expanded in size through mergers and acquisitions. By successively acquiring South Korean indie beauty brands — including Kraver Corporation, which owns Skin1004, as well as Tirtir and House of Huh — it established itself as a brand acquisition and development company. Its strategy of preserving the identity and product competitiveness of acquired brands while combining them with the group's global distribution network and digital marketing capabilities to rapidly boost overseas sales has paid off, according to assessments.
 Earnings growth is also steep. On a consolidated basis, 2025 revenue was 1.4718 trillion won (approximately $1.1 billion) and operating profit was 273.4 billion won (approximately $204.7 million), up 294% and 98% respectively from the prior year.

 Revenue 1.4718 trillion won (approximately $1.1 billion) 294% 
 Operating Profit 273.4 billion won (approximately $204.7 million) 98% 
 A company official said, "While preserving the unique identity and product competitiveness of acquired brands, we are using the group's global distribution and marketing infrastructure to support their entry into overseas markets," adding, "We plan to further refine the 'K-beauty value chain' that runs from brand discovery to acquisition, development and global distribution."
 Governance transparency and earnings sustainability are expected to emerge as key issues in the exchange's review. Goodai Global is accelerating governance restructuring to dispel concerns raised in some quarters about a "duplicate listing" (carve-out listing). The move follows controversy over duplicate listing after its key subsidiary Kraver Corporation initially pursued a separate listing on the Japanese stock market, while its parent Goodai Global opted for a direct KOSPI listing.
 Accordingly, Goodai Global has halted Kraver Corporation's plan for a separate listing in Japan. It is also coordinating exit options for financial investors (FIs), including agreements to sequentially buy the stakes of FIs that invested in the intermediate holding companies TM Beauty and Kraver Holdings.
 Challenges remain. In the course of aggressively expanding its footprint through M&A, Goodai Global raised funds through acquisition financing and large-scale convertible bond issuance, leaving it with a heavier financial cost burden. Whether it can generate synergies among its brands and secure stable cash generation is also cited as a variable that will determine its valuation after listing.
 The market is watching whether this listing can serve as a turning point for sentiment in South Korea's IPO market. If a valuation of up to 10 trillion won materializes, a large deal could emerge in this year's shrunken new-issue market and spur investor sentiment, according to observers. However, the gap between the valuation at the time of the pre-IPO round and the figures floated in the market, along with the financial cost burden, are expected to be key to the offering's success.
